items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: A lot of them, like John O’Hara, the novelist, and — he wrote Cannery Row.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well that was with Bobby Gordon and we just did a little, it wasn’t a tribute or anything. Eddie Condon was a kind of a catalyst for music that’s now just completely out of any of these jazz critics or these educators would not mention Eddie Condon. I mean they think he’s absolutely beneath them. It’s a guy who was a wonderful rhythm guitar player. He didn’t play any solos. What did he do? He drank himself crazy and he was just part of the times, but he was a wonderful catalyst. He brought together so many…
Harvard people and businessmen and that. But they liked it. They liked the sound. A lot of them, like John O’Hara, the novelist, and — he wrote Cannery Row.
